Definition: the eagle (or other large bird of prey)
BiblicalUsage: The eagle is the bird God uses to picture His own care: He bore Israel on eagles' wings and brought them to Himself. The law lists it among the birds not to be eaten, and David's song remembers Saul and Jonathan as swifter than eagles and stronger than lions.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the eagle says two things at once about God: He is high above me, and He carries me — His strength is the wings under my life. The law will not let me eat the eagle, but the promise lets me fly on its wings.
